about.title: About me
about.body:
Percy is a game designer and developer based in Calgary, Alberta. He believes in subtractive design and the power of simplicity in systems.

He focuses on clear, straightforward goals that retain players through a strong engaging core loop with a focus towards rewarding design thru data and systems that provides a fair challenge.

He enjoys breaking complex ideas down into clean, functional experiences, always aiming for clarity in communication and design. Outside of work, he is passionate about modding games and reverse engineering, and contributes to and maintains multiple active projects.

experience.body: Key contributor on Calamity VR, Echoes of Solera and Oren’s Adventures. Led design for multiple systems and developed internal authoring tools. Led design on UX/UI and defined the interaction language. Assisted with Unity implementation during prototyping.

Designed and developed multiple games and prototypes, assisted with level design and systems design. Lead game designer on Supercat, an action platformer built by five full-time developers and over ten contributors, and pitched its vertical slice in Edmonton and Calgary through the Indie Ignition Accelerator. Designed and built the Poly Punch VR prototype on an experimental Meta hand-tracking kit, and designed Lurk and Stick It at Knite Studios.

Designed product and content for brand partners, campaigns, CurseForge projects, in-game assets, major events and company identity. Built press and partner kits, and designed partner work that ran on CurseForge, Twitch, Modrinth and Lunar Client, used in programs with GamersOutreach, Project Hope and Tiltify. Also designed for Meloncube Hosting and Bisect Studios.
Designed Campaign and product design for a B2B security platform. Assisted with content strategy and production.
Led branding and motion design campaigns for mid-market and enterprise clients, mostly colleges, universities and companies. Assisted with art direction and production.

resume.title: Résumé
resume.subtitle: Game designer, user experience and player-focused systems
summary: Hi, I'm Percy, a game designer and developer in Calgary. I've made games and gaming content since I was 15, starting with custom assets and mods for Roblox, Unturned, and Minecraft. I began in computer science, then earned a bachelor's in Media, Graphics and Animation, where I built my first game and trained as a product designer. I founded Draconia and Kerberus, gaming networks that have served over 750,000 players in the past five years. I created Mythcraft (play as demigods), Dragoncraft (play as dragons), and the Kerberus Network.

✦ Shipped on Meta Quest, Itch.io, Curseforge, Roblox, Steam
✦ Founded Kerberus, served over 750,000+ players since 2017·
✦ Founded Smooth Brain Games, In Calgary with the help of Indie Ignition Accelerator
resume.philosophy:
Designing mechanics that are easy to learn but difficult to master

My background in user experience and product design influences how I design. I love building out prototypes using a rapid-development pipeline that lets me test out the mechanic and game feel before committing to anything. This also eliminates any communication gaps between design and engineering. Iteration and user feedback shapes every single piece of design I make, I believe in simplicity and first principles method of design. If you cannot defend your idea, it was a stupid idea anyways. Every mechanic within the game plays a role in keeping the game running or brings out certain emotions within the player. If your idea fails to do either, it’s not a priority. 

I lead the vision through design, improve communication, and find fun through simplicity. I keep designs clear and grounded in strong core systems and well-structured data, and I break complex ideas into clean, functional experiences, aiming for clarity in the gameplay and the process behind it. If my design can be interpreted by different people as different things, I have failed at clearly communicating myself hence its a bad design.

projects.title: Supercat
projects.description: Supercat is an action platformer where the player uses fluid movement combined with combat moves that complement the flow state to traverse levels and take down enemies.
contributions: Designed a modular movement kit with state-driven combat actions.
Built threats and challenges that allowed this kit to be utilized fully.
Blocked out tutorial levels that introduced mechanics through challenge.

sections.title: Movement and combat
sections.body: Wall-running, pouncing, slide-jumps, ramp hops and other mobility tools shared an interwoven surface with combat, which helped combat feel fluid. The goal was to achieve a flow state during combat.

media.alt: Supercat level blockout with arrows connecting a wall run, wall jump, slam, pounce, ramp hop and barrel slash into one movement route.

sections.title: Weapons and player state
sections.body: The same weapon changes behavior while sliding, airborne or grounded. This let me build momentum-based fighting combos that provided different uses for each weapon without overloading players with more inputs.

media.alt: Supercat character and mechanical claw concept sheet, created by Evalina Javorsky
Supercat first-person movement and claw attack storyboard

sections.title: Teaching through level design
sections.body: I used blockouts to introduce mechanics through the space itself, then gave players opportunities to try out different paths to achieve the goal by combining them in combat. There was always the recommended path, but curiosity was rewarded.

media.alt: Supercat level-design studies combining blockout views and movement spaces.

cards.title: Project Management
cards.body:
This project included a team of 5 full-time devs and over 10 contributors and commissioned artists.

It helped me learn how to plan, interact and coordinate between disciplines with talented artists, devs and designers to reach our goal with a first-principles approach.

cards.title: Pitching to Publishers
cards.body:
This project allowed me a chance to work with Indie Ignition Accelerator, pitch our vertical slice in Edmonton and Calgary at game fests and learn about the latter half of game development in detail.

Getting a game completed is a challenge but there is a lot more that goes into releasing it. The economics and logistics behind it are something I would have never learnt without this project.

cards.title: Team Leadership
cards.body:
As a multi-disciplinary designer, this project tested my leadership skills to the max. I excel at communicating between developers, artists and designers to understand and help meet their needs to make sure production goes uninterrupted. 

The massive team size combined with a huge pool of outside collaborators made leadership a real challenge, which I was happy to have faced early in my career as it taught me a lot.

cards.title: Systems Design
cards.body: In this project I was able to learn and expand my skill set as a multi-disciplinary designer. I had the opportunity and was trusted to establish key systems and work with other designers in its refinement and overseeing the balancing of said systems. I focused on an quicker iteration and improving ways to tweak, balance gameplay and removing friction in that process.

cards.title: Game Design (VR/AR)
cards.body: Designing for VR based on VR first principles and establishing frameworks to make interacting with the world feel more immersive was my goal. I focused on making combat and UX of the game feel integrated and take full advantage of the capabilities of the medium by utilizing unique mechanics which felt right in a spatial world.

cards.title: Playtesting and Tuning
cards.body: Hands on playtesting in engine, validating concepts and flows and iterating on this to bring values closer to our intended game feel was a major part of my process. With the clear hurdles in testing VR games unlike regular in-engine testing I designed tools with enabled testers to access dev menus from within the game and tweak changes and export said changes off the headset.

projects.title: Lurk
projects.description: A single-player first-person horror game set in an haunted 1800s house. where the player explores, solve puzzles, and uncovers the house's dark history.

hero.alt: Lurk horror game cover: a dim mansion staircase with the Lurk wordmark

contributions: Led design for the core loop which complimented the broader narrative of the game and build mini-games and puzzles which strengthened the premise.
Designed the puzzle, challenges and the mechanics to integrate with the environment to fit the environmental horror premise.
Created the level designs, triggers and volumes to affect global effects and lighting elements to play out the narrative beats

sections.title: Core loop
sections.body:
The player inherited a house from the 1800s, and as they explore they uncover the building's dark paranormal history .
The experience is built to be a narrative puzzle-solving where the player is constantly trapped and directed towards completing certain tasks while keeping their sanity in check.
Certain risky encounters leads to sanity drain and induce paranormal effects to the player which affects their perception of the world.

sections.title: Puzzles
sections.body:
Puzzle mechanics are deterministic and built on a set of rules and a probability system, so the house stays unpredictable across playthroughs without the puzzles themselves becoming unfair.
There are simpler fetch quests which ensure that story progression stays unaffected and the narrative remains serviceable.

sections.title: Spatial effects and lighting
sections.body:
Contributed towards the Level design and encounter. 
Worked in-engine on the lighting and optimization work for the level which included Draw calls reduction, LODs, light baking, Performance Profiling, Occlusion.
Designed shaders and assisted with technical art work carrying the visual language.
